episodes.title: The King Who Made Himself a Bridge
sources: Mahakapi Jataka (No. 407), in The Jataka, ed. E. B. Cowell, Vol. III, tr. H. T. Francis and R. A. Neil (Cambridge University Press, 1897), pp. 225-227; read 2026-11-16 at https://ancient-buddhist-texts.net/English-Texts/Jataka/407.htm
A. Cunningham, The Stupa of Bharhut (1879), plate XXXIII, fig. 4 (as cited in the translators' headnote to Jataka 407)

quiz.q: How did the troop cross the river?
quiz.why: The bamboo fell short, so he held a branch and made his own body the last span.

quiz.q: Which idea does the story stand for in an ethics answer?
options: Power is a duty to those you lead
A leader must never take risks
Loyalty is owed only to the ruler
quiz.why: The monkey king says the troop's happiness was his task; the king learns the same of his people.

quiz.q: Where is this scene carved in stone?
quiz.why: The video names the stupa at Bharhut, carved over two thousand years ago.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Retold lines: shots 11 and 12. Secondary-sourced: the Bharhut carving (cited from the translation's headnote). Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Rani ki Vav: Six Ideas in Stone
sources: UNESCO World Heritage List, entry 922, "Rani-ki-Vav (the Queen's Stepwell) at Patan, Gujarat", https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/922/ (read 2026-11-16)
World Heritage Committee, Decision 38 COM 8B.25 (Doha, 2014), https://whc.unesco.org/en/decisions/6111 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Why is Rani ki Vav called an inverted temple?
options: Its tower was built upside down
You go down towards water held sacred
It faces west instead of east
It was rebuilt after a flood
quiz.why: UNESCO describes it as designed as an inverted temple highlighting the sanctity of water.

quiz.q: What preserved its carving for centuries?
quiz.why: The Saraswati shifted and flood silt filled the stepwell, which kept the sculpture safe.

quiz.q: In which year was it put on UNESCO's World Heritage List?
quiz.why: It was inscribed in 2014, at the Committee's session in Doha.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none. The ASI page could not be reached; all facts are from UNESCO.

episodes.title: The Monsoon's Journey
sources: India Meteorological Department, press release "New normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of southwest monsoon over India" (April 2020), station table, https://mausam.imd.gov.in/backend/assets/press_release_pdf/IMD_Press_release_new_onset_and_withdrawal_dates%28Final%29.pdf (read 2026-11-16)
NCERT, Class XI, India: Physical Environment, ch. 4 "Climate"

quiz.q: Where does the monsoon normally arrive first on the mainland?
quiz.why: The normal onset over Kerala is 1 June; the video starts at Thiruvananthapuram.

quiz.q: Why does the Bay of Bengal branch move west up the Ganga plain?
quiz.why: Turned by the Arakan hills and then the Himalaya, it travels west along the Ganga plain.

quiz.q: By IMD's 2020 calendar, when does the monsoon normally cover the far north-west?
quiz.why: The new normal date is 8 July; the older calendar said 15 July.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: IMD normal onset dates are the 2020 revision, current as of 2026-11-16. Station dates for Goa, Guwahati, Varanasi, Lucknow and Jaipur were read from the IMD table and are worth re-checking.

episodes.title: I Am a Harappan Seal
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part I (Class XII), Theme 1 'Bricks, Beads and Bones', reprint 2020-21, sections 6, 7.1, 7.2, 10.1, 10.2 (archive.org/details/ncert-lehs1, read 2026-11-16)
John Marshall (ed.), Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization, Vol. I (1931), pp. 31-32 and 67-68 (archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.722, read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: How was a seal used to protect goods in trade?
options: It was hung around the trader's neck
It was pressed into wet clay on the knot of a tied sack
It was painted on the side of the boat
It was given to the buyer as payment
quiz.why: An unbroken sealing on the knot showed nobody had opened the sack, and who had sent it.

quiz.q: Why is the Harappan script thought not to be an alphabet?
options: It is written in Greek letters
It has too many signs, nearly 400
It was never written on seals
quiz.why: NCERT notes 375 to 400 signs: too many for letters standing for single sounds.

quiz.q: What stone were most Harappan seals cut from?
quiz.why: Seals were made of steatite, a soft stone, finished with a hard white coating.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Retold lines: none (the seal speaks in the first person as a device). Moving facts: 'still undeciphered' as of 2026-11-16.

episodes.title: The Bronze Dancer of Mohenjo-daro
sources: NCERT, An Introduction to Indian Art Part I (Class XI), ch. 2 'Arts of the Indus Valley', sections 'Bronze casting' and the 'Dancing Girl' caption (archive.org/details/ncert-kefa1, read 2026-11-16)
John Marshall (ed.), Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization, Vol. I (1931), pp. 33-34, 44-45 and plate notes to Pl. XCIV, 6-8 (archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.722, read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Which method was used to cast Harappan bronzes like the Dancing Girl?
quiz.why: A wax figure was coated in clay, the wax melted out, and molten metal poured into the hollow.

quiz.q: About how tall is the Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro?
quiz.why: NCERT calls her approximately four inches high; Marshall's plate note gives 4.25 inches.

quiz.q: Which of these was also cast in bronze by Indus craftspeople, as NCERT notes?
options: A buffalo with its head raised
quiz.why: NCERT names a buffalo with uplifted head and a goat among Indus bronzes.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Retold lines: none (the statuette speaks in the first person as a device). The sources disagree on the left hand, so the script does not describe it. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: The Emperor Who Regretted a War
sources: E. Hultzsch, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. I, Inscriptions of Asoka (1925; Varanasi reprint 1969), Rock Edict XIII, Shahbazgarhi version, translation, pp. 68-70 (read 2026-11-17)

quiz.q: How many years after his anointing did the king conquer Kalinga, according to Rock Edict XIII?
quiz.why: The edict opens: anointed eight years, Kalinga was conquered.

quiz.q: What does the edict call the principal conquest?
quiz.why: Section P: the conquest by morality is considered the principal one.

quiz.q: What does the edict say about the king's power after his repentance?
options: He kept it, and warned forest peoples of it
He handed it to the Cholas
quiz.why: Section N: they are told of his power 'in spite of repentance'.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. The identification of Devanampriya Priyadarshi with Ashoka is the standard scholarly view. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: The Village That Voted by Pot
sources: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, Studies in Cola History and Administration (Madras University Historical Series No. 7, 1932): translations of the two Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I (years 12 and 14), pp. 168-174; chronology table (A.D. 919 and 921)

quiz.q: How were the Uttaramerur committee members finally chosen?
options: By drawing pot-tickets, one name from each ward
quiz.why: The inscriptions describe pot-tickets drawn by a boy, one name per ward, read out before the Mahasabha.

quiz.q: How long did the committees serve?
quiz.why: Members served full three hundred and sixty days, then retired.

quiz.q: Who was barred from standing?
options: Anyone who had served and not shown accounts, and their close relatives
Anyone who lived near the tank
quiz.why: The settlement bars such members and their specified relatives.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. The inscriptions belong to a brahmadeya (caturvedimangalam) assembly, so eligibility was limited, and the video says it was open only to those who qualified. The CE dates are the author's conversion of regnal years. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: How a Chola Bronze Is Made
sources: NCERT, An Introduction to Indian Art Part I (Class XI Fine Art, 2020-21), ch. 7 'Indian Bronze Sculpture', pp. 104-108: the lost-wax process, Dancing Girl, Chola bronzes, Nataraja (archive.org ncert-kefa1, read 2026-11-17)

quiz.q: In lost-wax casting, what happens to the wax model?
options: It melts out of the clay mould as metal replaces it
It is kept inside the bronze
quiz.why: Heat melts the wax; the molten metal flows down the channel into its shape.

quiz.q: What coats the wax image before firing?
quiz.why: NCERT: a thick paste of equal parts clay, sand and cow-dung.

quiz.q: Which period produced some of the most beautiful South Indian bronzes?
quiz.why: NCERT credits the Chola period in Tamil Nadu, tenth to twelfth century.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. No deity is drawn; the Nataraja form is mentioned in words and by a ring-of-flames symbol only. The Dancing Girl's date is NCERT's. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Read a Temple in Sixty Seconds
sources: NCERT, An Introduction to Indian Art Part I (Class XI Fine Art, 2020-21), ch. 6 'Temple Architecture and Sculpture', pp. 70-87: basic form of the temple, Nagara, Dravida, Vesara (archive.org ncert-kefa1, read 2026-11-17)

quiz.q: Where is the garbhagriha placed in a Nagara temple?
quiz.why: NCERT: the garbhagriha is always located directly under the tallest tower.

quiz.q: What is the gateway in the front wall of a Dravida temple called?
quiz.why: The dravida temple is enclosed in a compound wall with a central gateway, the gopuram.

quiz.q: What is Vesara?
options: A hybrid of Nagara and Dravida features
quiz.why: A hybridised style popular after the mid-seventh century, notably in the Deccan.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. NCERT notes that the Vesara style is mentioned as independent by some scholars and that sub-styles are simplified. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: The Pillar That Hasn't Rusted
sources: J. F. Fleet, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. III (1888): translation of the Meharauli iron pillar inscription of Chandra, as reproduced in Wikipedia, 'Iron pillar of Delhi' (read 2026-11-17)
R. Balasubramaniam (IIT Kanpur), Current Science and Indian Journal of History of Science 36 (2001), on the passive protective film, summarised in Wikipedia, 'Iron pillar of Delhi' (read 2026-11-17)

quiz.q: Who is generally identified as the 'King Chandra' of the Delhi iron pillar inscription?
quiz.why: Script, style and place names point to the Gupta king Chandragupta II.

quiz.q: What helps the pillar resist rust?
options: A passive protective film on phosphorus-rich iron
quiz.why: Balasubramaniam explains a passive film at the iron-rust interface.

quiz.q: How was the pillar produced?
options: Forge-welded from pieces of wrought iron
quiz.why: It was made by forge welding of wrought iron pieces.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Both sources were read through a secondary page (Wikipedia), because the original papers were not reachable. The pillar speaks in the first person, which is a storytelling device. Retold lines: the verse about fame is a paraphrase of Fleet's translation. Moving facts: none.
